```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# the code of the benchmark is in two scripts in the directory code (one to
# simulate the tracks, one to run the benchmark), from which the chunks below
# are read
knitr::read_chunk("code/hr_benchmark_tracks.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/hr_packages_benchmark.R")
# amt is a suggested package, needed to simulate the example tracks
has_amt <- requireNamespace("amt", quietly = TRUE)
```

`tidytracks`, `amt` (Signer et al. 2019) and `adehabitatHR` (Calenge 2006)
can all estimate home ranges with minimum convex polygons (MCP), kernel
density estimation (KDE) and local convex hulls (LoCoH). This article
compares how long they take, on tracks simulated with `amt`, and checks
that, given the same settings, they give the same home ranges.

The benchmark takes about 35 minutes to run, so it was run once with the
script `vignettes/articles/code/hr_packages_benchmark.R` (in the source code
of the package), and its results are read here from the directory
`vignettes/articles/data`. It uses tracks simulated beforehand with the
script `vignettes/articles/code/hr_benchmark_tracks.R`, and stored in the
same directory, so it can be run again (e.g. on another machine) without
simulating them. The code shown below is taken from these two scripts.
Timings depend on the machine (see
[Machine and software](#machine-and-software)), but the differences between
the packages should be similar on other machines.

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
```

```{r results_packages, message = FALSE}
# to summarise and plot the results
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Simulating tracks with amt

`amt` can simulate movement from an integrated step selection function
(iSSF; Avgar et al. 2016), which combines a movement kernel (the
distributions of step lengths and turning angles) with the selection of
the places where steps end. To get tracks that stay within a home range,
the selection decreases with the squared distance from a centre:

```{r simulate-track, eval = has_amt}
```

For example, the first three tracks of the first data set below:

```{r example_tracks, eval = has_amt}
example_tracks <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  simulate_track(
    id = sprintf("medium_%03d", i),
    n_locations = 500,
    seed = 1000 + i
  )
})
example_tracks <- do.call(rbind, example_tracks)
```

```{r plot_example_tracks, eval = has_amt, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3}
ggplot(example_tracks, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_path(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~id) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

# The data sets

We simulate two data sets, with the same model: many tracks of medium
length, and a few long tracks (with one location per hour, about three
weeks and fourteen months of tracking respectively):

```{r simulate-datasets, eval = FALSE}
```

Simulating the tracks takes about 8 minutes on 4 cores: each step takes
about 10 ms, mostly in the bookkeeping of `amt` rather than in the simulation
itself. So the tracks were simulated once (with `code/hr_benchmark_tracks.R`) and
stored in `data/hr_benchmark_tracks.rds`, from which the benchmark reads
them:

```{r read-tracks, eval = FALSE}
```

# Running the estimators

Each package works on its own class of objects: a `move2` object for
`tidytracks`, a `track_xy` for `amt` and a `SpatialPointsDataFrame` (from
`sp`) for `adehabitatHR`. These are built from the data frame of each data
set (outside of the timings):

```{r inputs, eval = FALSE}
```

The KDEs are estimated on the same grid for all the packages:

```{r grid, eval = FALSE}
```

The home ranges are then estimated with each method and package, at the 50%
and 95% levels. `tidytracks` and `adehabitatHR` estimate the home ranges of
all the tracks in one call; `amt` estimates the home range of a single track,
so its estimators are applied to each track in turn, after nesting the
tracks as shown in the documentation of `amt`:

```{r estimators, eval = FALSE}
```

The settings are matched so that the packages estimate the same home ranges:

- **MCP**: all three packages exclude the locations farthest from the mean
  of the locations, and build the convex hull of the others.
- **KDE**: all three use a bivariate normal kernel, with the reference
  bandwidth of each track (\(h = \sqrt{(\sigma^2_x + \sigma^2_y)/2} \, n^{-1/6}\)),
  on the same grid. The UDs are timed on their own (`kde_ud`), and with
  their isopleths (`kde_iso`, i.e. from the locations to the isopleths).
  `tidytracks` (with `MASS::kde2d()`) and `adehabitatHR` evaluate the kernel
  of every location at the centre of every cell, whilst `amt` (with
  `KernSmooth::bkde2D()`) first bins the locations onto the grid, which is
  faster but approximate.
- **LoCoH**: hulls of each location and its 10 nearest neighbours (`n = 10`
  in `tidytracks` and `amt`, `k = 11` in `adehabitatHR`, which counts the
  location itself). For each level, the isopleth is the union of the
  smallest hulls whose coverage (the proportion of locations in the hulls)
  is closest to the level.

Each estimator is run once, and, if that took less than a minute, five more
times, of which the median time is reported:

```{r timing, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r run-benchmark, eval = FALSE}
```

The areas of the home ranges are then extracted from the results of each
package (with the functions in `areas`, in the script). `LoCoH.k()` from
`adehabitatHR` is not run on the long tracks: it would take hours (see
[LoCoH on a single track](#locoh-on-a-single-track)).

# Do the packages give the same home ranges?

For each method, data set and level, we compare the area of the home range of
each track from `amt` and `adehabitatHR` with the area from `tidytracks`:

```{r read_areas}
area_results <- read.csv("data/hr_benchmark_areas.csv")
area_diff <- area_results %>%
  filter(package != "tidytracks") %>%
  inner_join(
    area_results %>%
      filter(package == "tidytracks") %>%
      select(dataset, method, id, level, area_tidytracks = area),
    by = c("dataset", "method", "id", "level")
  ) %>%
  # the relative difference, in %
  mutate(diff = 100 * abs(area / area_tidytracks - 1)) %>%
  group_by(method, package, level) %>%
  summarise(
    median_diff = median(diff),
    max_diff = max(diff),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r table_areas, echo = FALSE}
area_diff %>%
  mutate(
    method = recode(
      method,
      mcp = "MCP",
      kde_iso = "KDE",
      locoh = "LoCoH"
    ),
    level = paste0(100 * level, "%"),
    across(
      c(median_diff, max_diff),
      ~ case_when(
        .x == 0 ~ "0",
        .x < 0.001 ~ "< 0.001",
        TRUE ~ formatC(signif(.x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(method, c("MCP", "KDE", "LoCoH")), package, level) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Method", "Package", "Level",
      "Median difference (%)", "Largest difference (%)"
    ),
    align = "lllrr"
  )
```

MCP and LoCoH give the same home ranges in all three packages (the tiny
differences for LoCoH in `amt` come from its buffering of each hull by
0.00001 m). The KDE isopleths of `adehabitatHR` are within 0.1% of those of
`tidytracks`: both evaluate the same kernels at the same points, and differ
only in how they draw the isopleths from the UDs. Those of `amt` differ by
about 1%, as it approximates the KDE by binning the locations.

# How long do they take?

```{r read_timings}
timings <- read.csv("data/hr_benchmark_timings.csv")
# labels for the plots and tables
method_labels <- c(
  mcp = "MCP",
  kde_ud = "KDE: UD",
  kde_iso = "KDE: isopleths",
  locoh = "LoCoH"
)
package_levels <- c("tidytracks", "amt", "adehabitatHR")
timings <- timings %>%
  mutate(
    data_set = paste(
      tracks, "tracks of",
      format(locations, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "locations"
    ),
    data_set = factor(data_set, unique(data_set)),
    method = factor(method_labels[method], method_labels),
    package = factor(package, package_levels)
  )
```

```{r timing_ratios, include = FALSE}
# the time taken by a package, and relative to tidytracks, for the text
time_of <- function(dataset, method, package) {
  timings$seconds[
    timings$dataset == dataset &
      timings$method == method_labels[[method]] &
      timings$package == package
  ]
}
ratio <- function(dataset, method, package) {
  signif(
    time_of(dataset, method, package) /
      time_of(dataset, method, "tidytracks"),
    2
  )
}
```

```{r plot_timings, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
# one colour per package (and its name on the y axis)
package_colours <- c(
  tidytracks = "#2a78d6",
  amt = "#eb6834",
  adehabitatHR = "#1baf7a"
)
ggplot(timings, aes(x = seconds, y = package, colour = package)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # the combinations that were not run
  geom_text(
    data = timings %>%
      complete(data_set, method, package) %>%
      filter(is.na(seconds)),
    aes(x = 1, label = "not run"),
    colour = "grey40",
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_grid(method ~ data_set) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000),
    labels = c("0.1", "1", "10", "100", "1000")
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = package_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Time (s, log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "lines"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)
  )
```

```{r table_timings, echo = FALSE}
timings %>%
  select(data_set, method, package, seconds) %>%
  arrange(package) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = package, values_from = seconds) %>%
  mutate(across(
    any_of(package_levels),
    ~ ifelse(
      is.na(.x),
      "not run",
      formatC(signif(.x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")
    )
  )) %>%
  arrange(data_set, method) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Data set", "Method", package_levels),
    align = "llrrr",
    caption = "Time (s) to estimate the home ranges of all the tracks."
  )
```

- **MCP** takes at most about a second in all three packages. `tidytracks`
  is the fastest: `amt` takes `r ratio("medium", "mcp", "amt")` times as long
  on the medium tracks, and `adehabitatHR` `r ratio("medium", "mcp",
  "adehabitatHR")` times (`r ratio("long", "mcp", "adehabitatHR")` times on
  the long tracks).
- **KDE**: `tidytracks` and `adehabitatHR` evaluate the kernel of every
  location in every cell of the grid, which takes a time proportional to the
  number of locations times the number of cells, whilst `amt` first bins
  the locations onto the grid, so that its time hardly depends on the number
  of locations. For the UDs of the medium tracks, `tidytracks` and `amt`
  take about the same time, and `adehabitatHR` `r ratio("medium", "kde_ud",
  "adehabitatHR")` times as long; for the long tracks, `amt` is
  `r signif(1 / ratio("long", "kde_ud", "amt"), 2)` times faster than
  `tidytracks`, at the cost of its approximation. Drawing the isopleths, on
  the other hand, adds little to the time of `tidytracks`
  (`r signif(time_of("medium", "kde_iso", "tidytracks") - time_of("medium", "kde_ud", "tidytracks"), 1)` s
  for the 100 medium tracks), but more to those of `amt`
  (`r signif(time_of("medium", "kde_iso", "amt") - time_of("medium", "kde_ud", "amt"), 1)` s)
  and `adehabitatHR`
  (`r signif(time_of("medium", "kde_iso", "adehabitatHR") - time_of("medium", "kde_ud", "adehabitatHR"), 2)` s).
  From the locations to the isopleths, `tidytracks` is thus the fastest for
  many tracks of medium length (`amt` takes
  `r ratio("medium", "kde_iso", "amt")` times as long, and `adehabitatHR`
  `r ratio("medium", "kde_iso", "adehabitatHR")` times), and `amt` for a few
  long tracks (`r signif(1 / ratio("long", "kde_iso", "amt"), 2)` times
  faster than `tidytracks`). Most of the time of `tidytracks` on long tracks
  is spent in a matrix product (in `MASS::kde2d()`), which an optimised BLAS
  (such as OpenBLAS) can make several times faster; this benchmark used the
  reference BLAS of R.
- **LoCoH**: `tidytracks` is the fastest, by far: `amt` takes
  `r ratio("medium", "locoh", "amt")` to `r ratio("long", "locoh", "amt")`
  times as long, and `adehabitatHR`
  `r ratio("medium", "locoh", "adehabitatHR")` times as long on the medium
  tracks (`r round(time_of("medium", "locoh", "adehabitatHR") / 60)` minutes,
  against `r signif(time_of("medium", "locoh", "tidytracks"), 2)` s).

# LoCoH on a single track

```{r read_scaling}
locoh_scaling <- read.csv("data/hr_benchmark_locoh_scaling.csv") %>%
  mutate(package = factor(package, package_levels))
```

```{r plot_scaling, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(locoh_scaling, aes(x = locations, y = seconds, colour = package)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  # each line labelled at its last point
  geom_text(
    data = locoh_scaling %>%
      group_by(package) %>%
      filter(locations == max(locations)),
    aes(label = package),
    hjust = 0,
    # in log10 units, as the x axis is on a log scale
    nudge_x = 0.06,
    colour = "grey20",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000),
    labels = c("500", "1,000", "2,000", "5,000", "10,000"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.3))
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100),
    labels = c("0.1", "1", "10", "100")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = package_colours) +
  labs(
    x = "Locations (log scale)",
    y = "Time (s, log scale)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
```

```{r extrapolation, include = FALSE}
# adehabitatHR on 2000 locations, and extrapolated to 10,000 locations,
# assuming that its time grows with the square of the number of locations
ade_2000 <- locoh_scaling$seconds[
  locoh_scaling$package == "adehabitatHR" & locoh_scaling$locations == 2000
]
ade_10000 <- ade_2000 * (10000 / 2000)^2
```

The time taken by `tidytracks` and `amt` grows about linearly with the
number of locations, whilst that of `adehabitatHR`, which computes the
distances between all pairs of locations (in R), roughly quadruples each time
the number of locations doubles. A track of 10,000 locations would thus take
it about `r round(ade_10000 / 60, -1)` minutes, and the 10 long tracks about
`r round(10 * ade_10000 / 3600)` hours, against
`r signif(locoh_scaling$seconds[locoh_scaling$package == "tidytracks" & locoh_scaling$locations == 10000], 1)` s
per track for `tidytracks`.

# Summary

- Given the same settings, the three packages give the same MCP and LoCoH
  home ranges, and KDE isopleths within 0.1% (`tidytracks` and
  `adehabitatHR`) or about 1% (`amt`, which approximates the KDE).
- `tidytracks` is the fastest for MCP and LoCoH (more than 10 times faster
  than `amt`, and more than 100 times faster than `adehabitatHR`, for
  LoCoH), and for the KDE isopleths of many tracks.
- For the KDE of long tracks, `amt` is the fastest, thanks to its binned
  approximation; `tidytracks` computes the exact KDE, slightly faster than
  `adehabitatHR`.
- LoCoH in `adehabitatHR` becomes impractical beyond a few thousand
  locations per track.
